<div class="note">
<span class="lab">What this produces</span>
<p>One named biological concept recovered across three cohorts that share no individual, with the
effect it has in each modality, a p-value that accounts for the whole vocabulary, a statement of
whether more than one modality was needed, a table of coordinated variation the vocabulary cannot
name, and a set of controls.</p>
</div>

## Before you start

```r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("lescailab/chorale")
library(chorale)
```

R 4.4 or later. Bioconductor dependencies resolve through `BiocManager`. Two optional packages widen
what the pipeline can do: `msigdbr` supplies curated concept definitions, and `rgoslin` parses lipid
shorthand names. Neither is needed for this tutorial.

## Step 1. Three cohorts with no individual in common

The modalities are measured on different individuals, so what connects them is a fixed vocabulary of
named biological concepts: a concept is a set of features that belong together for a stated
biological reason, and every modality is scored on the same concepts. The collection below is built
so that one named concept, sphingolipid metabolism, really does separate cases from controls in all
three cohorts.

```r
set.seed(1)

gene_ids <- sprintf("gene_%04d", seq_len(400))
sets <- list(
  REACTOME_SPHINGOLIPID_METABOLISM = gene_ids[1:80],
  REACTOME_PHOSPHOLIPID_METABOLISM = gene_ids[101:180],
  REACTOME_NEURONAL_SYSTEM         = gene_ids[201:280],
  REACTOME_INNATE_IMMUNE_SYSTEM    = gene_ids[301:380]
)

# A lipidome is reported in shorthand, as every lipidomics platform does.
lipid_names <- function(classes, n_each) {
  unlist(lapply(classes, function(cl) sprintf("%s %d:1;O2", cl, 30:(30 + n_each - 1))))
}
sphingo   <- lipid_names(c("SM", "Cer", "HexCer", "AHexCer"), 15)
lipid_ids <- c(sphingo, lipid_names(c("PC", "PE", "PI", "TG"), 15))

cohort <- function(prefix, n, features, raised, effect, private = 20) {
  sample_id <- sprintf("%s_%03d", prefix, seq_len(n))
  phenotype <- rep(c("control", "case"), length.out = n)
  sex       <- rep(c("F", "F", "M", "M"), length.out = n)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(length(features) * n), nrow = length(features),
              dimnames = list(features, sample_id))
  x[raised, phenotype == "case"] <- x[raised, phenotype == "case"] + effect
  # A cohort-specific direction on features no concept covers.
  tail_at <- seq(length(features) - private + 1L, length(features))
  x[tail_at, ] <- x[tail_at, ] +
    matrix(rep(rnorm(n), each = private), nrow = private)
  chorale_load(x, data.frame(sample_id = sample_id, phenotype = phenotype,
                             sex = sex, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
}

containers <- list(
  RNA   = cohort("rna",   120, gene_ids,  sets[[1]], effect = 0.8),
  PROT  = cohort("prot",   90, gene_ids,  sets[[1]], effect = 0.7),
  METAB = cohort("metab",  80, lipid_ids, sphingo,   effect = 0.9)
)

length(Reduce(intersect, lapply(containers, colnames)))
#> [1] 0
```

Zero individuals in common. That is the situation the package is for.

<div class="note">
<span class="lab">Requirement</span>
<p>Two columns are required: <code>sample_id</code>, matching the assay columns in order, and
<code>phenotype</code>, on at least two levels. The phenotype is a condition of entry, not a
covariate: the quantity being estimated is a contrast, so a modality that cannot express one cannot
contribute to it and the fit stops with an error naming it. Every other column is a covariate the
effect is adjusted for wherever the modalities share it, and nothing needs declaring in advance.
Labels are resolved as the data are read, so a cohort recording controls as <code>WT</code> and
another as <code>control</code> still share a level. The <a href="../input-format">input data</a>
page sets this out in full, and <code>chorale_check_design()</code> reports what a collection can
anchor on before it is fitted.</p>
</div>

`chorale_load()` puts each modality into a `SummarizedExperiment`, Bioconductor's structure for a
feature-by-sample assay with its sample annotation, so the measurements and the sample table cannot
be subset or reordered out of alignment. It also maps blank strings and placeholder values to
missing, since a covariate holding `""` beside one real level would otherwise present as a two-level
contrast.

```r
containers$RNA
#> class: SummarizedExperiment
#> dim: 400 120
#> assays(1): counts
#> rownames(400): gene_0001 gene_0002 ... gene_0399 gene_0400
#> colnames(120): rna_001 rna_002 ... rna_119 rna_120
#> colData names(3): sample_id phenotype sex
```

## Step 2. Fix the vocabulary and read its coverage

Genes and proteins reach a concept through their identifiers. Lipid species reach the same concept
through their class, using a table shipped with the package, so a lipidome and a transcriptome end
up in one vocabulary rather than in two that have to be reconciled afterwards. Which modality is a
lipidome is declared, because a wrong guess would silently leave it out.

```r
concepts <- chorale_concepts(containers, sets,
                             feature_space = c(METAB = "lipid"),
                             min_features = 5)
concepts
#> <chorale_concepts>
#>   modalities: RNA, PROT, METAB
#>   concepts supplied: 4
#>   expressible in every modality: 2
#>   expressible in some but not all: 2
#>   expressible in none: 0
#>   in the vocabulary (at least 1 modalities): 4
#>   features a modality needs for a concept: 5
#>     RNA          4 concepts
#>     PROT         4 concepts
#>     METAB        2 concepts
```

On real data this is the first thing to read. Coverage is per concept and per modality:

```r
concepts$coverage
#>                             concept modality n_features expressed
#> 1  REACTOME_SPHINGOLIPID_METABOLISM      RNA         80      TRUE
#> 2  REACTOME_SPHINGOLIPID_METABOLISM     PROT         80      TRUE
#> 3  REACTOME_SPHINGOLIPID_METABOLISM    METAB         60      TRUE
#> 4  REACTOME_PHOSPHOLIPID_METABOLISM      RNA         80      TRUE
#> 5  REACTOME_PHOSPHOLIPID_METABOLISM     PROT         80      TRUE
#> 6  REACTOME_PHOSPHOLIPID_METABOLISM    METAB         15      TRUE
#> 7          REACTOME_NEURONAL_SYSTEM      RNA         80      TRUE
#> 8          REACTOME_NEURONAL_SYSTEM     PROT         80      TRUE
#> 9          REACTOME_NEURONAL_SYSTEM    METAB          0     FALSE
#> 10    REACTOME_INNATE_IMMUNE_SYSTEM      RNA         80      TRUE
#> 11    REACTOME_INNATE_IMMUNE_SYSTEM     PROT         80      TRUE
#> 12    REACTOME_INNATE_IMMUNE_SYSTEM    METAB          0     FALSE
```

Two concepts reach all three modalities and two reach only the gene-based pair, because no lipid
class takes part in them. Those two will be tested across two modalities rather than three, which is
a statement about the measured features and not a failure.

## Step 3. Fit

```r
fit <- chorale_concept_fit(containers, concepts, n_free = 2,
                           n_permutations = 999, n_init = 10, seed = 1)
fit
#> <chorale_concept_fit>
#>   modalities: RNA, PROT, METAB
#>   concepts in the vocabulary: 4 (2 expressible in every modality)
#>   free dimensions: RNA 2, PROT 2, METAB 2
#>   concepts supported at q <= 0.05 : 1
#>   strongest: REACTOME_SPHINGOLIPID_METABOLISM (z = 64.54)
```

Three things happen in that call, in a fixed order. Every modality is scored on the vocabulary,
without the design being consulted. The concept scores are projected out and what remains becomes
free dimensions. Only then is the design asked whether each concept separates cases from controls.

How much of each modality the two channels account for:

```r
fit$encoding$variance[, c("modality", "n_concepts", "n_free", "concept_share",
                          "free_share", "residual_share")]
#>       modality n_concepts n_free concept_share free_share residual_share
#> RNA        RNA          4      2        0.0680     0.0520         0.8800
#> PROT      PROT          4      2        0.0753     0.0612         0.8635
#> METAB    METAB          2      2        0.1786     0.0792         0.7422
```

The three shares partition the variance of the analysis matrix. Most of it is feature-level noise,
as it is in any bulk assay; the concept channel holds what the vocabulary reaches and the free
dimensions hold the largest coordinated directions left over.

### Choosing the number of free dimensions

`n_free = "auto"`, the default, selects the count by reproducibility. The decomposition is run
repeatedly at each candidate count, from different initialisations and on subsamples of the samples,
components are matched one to one, and the largest count at which the weakest component still clears
a declared threshold is taken. Parallel analysis supplies the upper bound.

```r
auto <- chorale_encode(containers, concepts, n_free = "auto", n_init = 10)
auto$encodings$RNA$selection
```

The table it returns carries one row per candidate count, with the weakest matched correlation
across initialisations and across subsamples, and whether that count is admissible. Reading it
matters more than the number: a count whose weakest component reproduces at 0.98 across subsamples
is a different object from one that reproduces at 0.6.

## Step 4. Read the concepts

```r
fit$evidence$joint[, c("concept", "n_modalities", "modalities", "joint_z",
                       "sign_agreement", "heterogeneity_p", "q_value",
                       "p_family")]
#>                            concept n_modalities       modalities joint_z
#> 1 REACTOME_SPHINGOLIPID_METABOLISM            3 METAB, PROT, RNA 64.5351
#> 2 REACTOME_PHOSPHOLIPID_METABOLISM            3 METAB, PROT, RNA  0.4023
#> 3         REACTOME_NEURONAL_SYSTEM            2        PROT, RNA -0.3398
#> 4    REACTOME_INNATE_IMMUNE_SYSTEM            2        PROT, RNA  0.1401
#>   sign_agreement heterogeneity_p q_value p_family
#> 1          1.000          0.9777  0.0000    0.001
#> 2          0.667          0.1370  0.8894    0.992
#> 3          0.500          0.3722  0.8894    0.998
#> 4          0.500          0.5583  0.8894    1.000
```

One concept is supported. Four columns decide how much that is worth.

`joint_z` combines the modalities by inverse-variance weighting, so effects in opposite directions
cancel. `sign_agreement` of 1.000 says all three modalities move the same way, which is what makes
the finding shared rather than one modality carrying the others. `heterogeneity_p` of 0.98 says the
three effects are consistent with one underlying quantity. `p_family` compares the concept with the
largest statistic anywhere in the vocabulary under permuted phenotypes, and 0.001 is the smallest
value 999 permutations can produce.

The effect in each modality is where the size of the finding is read:

```r
fit$evidence$per_modality[, c("concept", "modality", "n_features", "effect",
                              "se", "z")]
#>                             concept modality n_features   effect     se       z
#> 2  REACTOME_SPHINGOLIPID_METABOLISM      RNA         80  1.92820 0.0461 41.8476
#> 6  REACTOME_SPHINGOLIPID_METABOLISM     PROT         80  1.91542 0.0574 33.3659
#> 10 REACTOME_SPHINGOLIPID_METABOLISM    METAB         60  1.93108 0.0536 36.0599
```

The effect is in standard deviations of the concept score, adjusted for the covariates the
modalities share. Cases sit about 1.9 standard deviations above controls on sphingolipid metabolism
in each of the three cohorts, which were measured on different animals and on three different
platforms.

## Step 5. Separate a concept from its neighbourhood

Curated concepts share features, so a signal in one appears in every concept overlapping it. Each
concept is therefore reported again with its overlapping neighbours regressed out.

```r
fit$evidence$joint[, c("concept", "joint_z", "max_jaccard", "attributed_z")]
#>                            concept joint_z max_jaccard attributed_z
#> 1 REACTOME_SPHINGOLIPID_METABOLISM 64.5351           0      64.5351
```

`max_jaccard` is zero here because the four concepts were built disjoint. On curated collections it
is rarely zero, and a concept whose `attributed_z` collapses while `joint_z` stays large is
reporting the neighbourhood it sits in rather than itself.

## Step 6. Ask whether more than one modality was needed

```r
chorale_added_value(fit)[, c("concept", "n_modalities", "joint_z",
                             "best_single_z", "margin", "needs_multiple")]
#>                            concept n_modalities joint_z best_single_z margin
#> 1 REACTOME_SPHINGOLIPID_METABOLISM            3 64.5351       41.8476 22.688
#> 2    REACTOME_INNATE_IMMUNE_SYSTEM            2  0.1401        0.4898 -0.350
#> 3         REACTOME_NEURONAL_SYSTEM            2 -0.3398        0.8399 -0.500
#> 4 REACTOME_PHOSPHOLIPID_METABOLISM            3  0.4023        1.5820 -1.180
#>   needs_multiple
#> 1           TRUE
```

The margin is the combined statistic less the best any single modality reached. A positive margin is
what separates a result integration produced from a result one modality produced and the others
accompanied.

## Step 7. Look outside the vocabulary

```r
chorale_free_dimensions(fit, n_permutations = 999)[
  , c("modality", "dimension", "variance_share", "reproducibility", "z",
      "p_family", "outside_vocabulary")]
#>   modality dimension variance_share reproducibility       z p_family
#> 1      RNA    free_2         0.0260           0.943 -0.2794        1
#> 2    METAB    free_2         0.0396           0.969  0.2635        1
#> 3     PROT    free_2         0.0306           1.000  0.1688        1
#> 4     PROT    free_1         0.0306           1.000  0.1120        1
#> 5    METAB    free_1         0.0396           0.969  0.1010        1
#> 6      RNA    free_1         0.0260           0.943 -0.0186        1
#>   outside_vocabulary
#> 1              FALSE
```

Nothing outside the vocabulary moves with the phenotype in this collection, which is correct: the
cohort-specific direction built into the tail features was drawn independently of the phenotype. A
row with `outside_vocabulary` true would be coordinated variation the vocabulary has no name for, and
the table names the features loading on it so it can be followed up.

## Step 8. Run the controls

```r
controls <- chorale_null(fit, containers, n_shuffles = 20)
controls
#> <chorale_concept_null>
#>   concepts supported at q <= 0.05 : 1
#>   strongest concept statistic: 64.535
#>   phenotype permutation    p = 0.001 (smallest attainable 0.001, 999 resamples)
#>   modality shuffle         not applicable: modalities share fewer than ten features
#>   initialisation stability weakest component 0.829
```

The phenotype permutation reuses the concept scores, since permuting the design leaves the assay
untouched: the permutation count is a choice about resolution rather than about what a refit can
afford. The modality shuffle needs a shared feature space, which a transcriptome and a lipidome do
not have, so it is declared inapplicable rather than quietly passed. Every control states the
smallest p-value it can attain, so one that cannot reach the threshold it is read against is visible
as one.

<div class="note warn">
<span class="lab">Permutation count</span>
<p>The smallest p-value <code>B</code> permutations can produce is <code>1/(B+1)</code>. Set the
count from the resolution the report needs, and read it back from the control table before quoting
any p-value.</p>
</div>

## Step 9. Write the report

```r
out <- chorale_report(fit, null = controls, path = "results/chorale")
basename(out)
#>  [1] "concepts.tsv"             "concept_effects.tsv"
#>  [3] "concept_coverage.tsv"     "variance.tsv"
#>  [5] "concept_variance.tsv"     "free_dimensions.tsv"
#>  [7] "added_value.tsv"          "controls.tsv"
#>  [9] "concept_scores_RNA.tsv"   "free_scores_RNA.tsv"
#> [11] "concept_scores_PROT.tsv"  "free_scores_PROT.tsv"
#> [13] "concept_scores_METAB.tsv" "free_scores_METAB.tsv"
#> [15] "report.html"
```

`report.html` leads with the concept table and explains which controls were run. The
[outputs page](../outputs) documents every column.

## Using your own data

The workflow above changes in three places.

**Reading the data.** Each modality is a features-by-samples numeric matrix and a design table with
one row per column of the matrix.

```r
mat    <- as.matrix(read.delim("data/RNA_matrix.tsv", row.names = 1))
design <- read.delim("data/RNA_design.tsv")
se     <- chorale_load(mat, design)
```

**Identifiers and the vocabulary.** Map transcripts and proteins into one identifier space, then
retrieve the concepts for the species under study.

```r
feature_map <- list(
  RNA  = chorale_map(rownames(mat_rna),  from = "ENSEMBL"),
  PROT = chorale_map(rownames(mat_prot), from = "UNIPROT")
)
sets <- chorale_genesets(c("hallmark", "reactome"), species = "Mus musculus")
fit  <- chorale_concept_fit(containers, sets, feature_map = feature_map,
                            feature_space = c(METAB = "lipid"))
```

**Inputs to avoid.** A cross-modality harmonised matrix puts information into the scores that the
design is then asked to find in them. Keep study and batch as covariates in the design instead.

## When something does not work

| Symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `No concept reaches ... features` | The vocabulary does not reach the measured features | Check identifier mapping, and read `chorale_concepts()` coverage before fitting |
| A modality expresses no concept | A lipidome was not declared with `feature_space` | Declare it, and check `concepts$coverage` for that modality |
| Error naming a modality without a phenotype contrast | A design lacks `phenotype`, or it takes one value once blanks are mapped to missing | Resolve the phenotype for that modality, or drop it |
| Every concept has `n_modalities` of 1 | Cohorts record a covariate under labels the registry does not cover, or the vocabularies do not overlap | Run `chorale_check_design()`, then extend `chorale_label_registry()` |
| No concept supported | The evidence did not beat the null | A real outcome. Report it, and read the coverage and free-dimension tables |
| Concepts supported but `attributed_z` collapses | The signal belongs to an overlapping neighbour | Report the neighbourhood rather than the concept |
